title: Request-scoped telemetry adapter with pluggable context serializers
creator: Elena Park
description:
Summary:

We need a lightweight request-scoped telemetry adapter that SDKs and middleware can use to attach tracing and metadata without forcing a single propagation format across all services. Goals: low CPU/memory overhead on hot paths, deterministic header normalization, support for multiple serializers (W3C traceparent+baggage, custom compact binary for edge SDKs, and an internal 'opaque' envelope), and a gradual rollout plan that allows opt-in for existing SDKs.

Why now:

Recent production incidents showed inconsistent trace stitching between edge proxies and backend runtimes where agents used different propagation encodings, causing orphan spans and loss of request-level metrics. This ticket builds a pluggable adapter that standardizes how we encode/decode request context in the SDKs and edge middleware while remaining extensible for future serializers (e.g., signed provenance stamps).

Design notes:

- Adapter is a minimal abstraction: RequestTelemetryAdapter with methods: attachContext(headers, ctx), extractContext(headers) -> ctx, serialize(ctx, format), deserialize(bytes, format).
- Pluggable serializers implement a small trait (serialize/deserialize, stable id string, cost_hint). We ship three serializers initially: w3c, compact-binary-v1 (for low-latency edge SDKs), and opaque-envelope-v1 (internal fallback for RDWD runtime).
- Header normalization layer: single canonical header map used for lookups to avoid duplicated keys (case-insensitive, strip hop-by-hop headers).
- Backwards compatibility: when extracting, attempt ordered deserializers: w3c -> compact-binary -> opaque. When attaching, default to the configured primary serializer for the route; support additional negotiation header `x-rw-ctx-formats` to advertise supported formats during canary phases.
- Performance: avoid allocations on hot path where possible. Serializer API supports zero-copy for binary formats and provides a small pre-allocated buffer hint. The adapter should expose a fast-path: if context is already cached on the request object, skip deserialize/serialize.

Acceptance criteria:

- Implement adapter and three serializers in the runtime SDK with feature flag `rw.telemetry.adapter=v1`.
- Add middleware shim for edge-proxy to use adapter for both incoming and outgoing requests.
- Unit + integration tests for format negotiation and canonical header mapping.
- Microbenchmarks: additional CPU overhead <= 2% p50 request step for common request sizes; allocation delta < 128 bytes median.
- Rollout strategy documented and validated: start with internal services, then 10% traffic canary, then full.
- Dashboard panels added to Console showing: percent of requests decoded successfully, format mix over time, drop rate due to malformed context.

Implementation plan:

1) Library scaffolding: trait + adapter + no-op implementation (2d).
2) Implement W3C serializer using existing trace id/span id code (1d).
3) Implement compact-binary-v1 serializer with small TLV layout optimized for header length (3d).
4) Implement opaque-envelope-v1 serializer (2d).
5) Header normalization util and caching on request objects (2d).
6) Edge-proxy middleware integration + canary header support (3d).
7) Add telemetry metrics and Console panels (2d).
8) Benchmarks and performance tuning (2d).

Risks and tradeoffs:

- Each serializer increases parsing work; to mitigate we rely on short-circuit cache and prioritized deserializers.
- Negotiation header adds a small header size increase; it's only active during canary rollout.
- Rolling out a new adapter to many SDKs may surface subtle nil/None differences in baggage semantics; we will provide clear migration guidance and a compatibility mode that maps unknown baggage values to a reserved slot.

Migration and rollout:

- Phase 0: library in repo behind feature flag, unit tests only.
- Phase 1: enable for internal services in runtime staging for 1 week. Collect decode success metric and format mix.
- Phase 2: enable in edge-proxy for 10% of traffic with `x-rw-ctx-formats` negotiation header. Monitor orphan-span rate, decode failures, latency tail.
- Phase 3: full rollout, flip feature flag org-wide, deprecate old fortify middleware after 30 days.

Monitoring & dashboards:

- Console panels to add: "Context Decode Success Rate", "Context Format Distribution", "Orphan Span Ratio", "Inbound Serialization Latency p50/p95", "Decode Failure Samples".
- Create alert: decode_success_rate < 99.5% over 5m for core services -> page on-call and roll back canary.

Open questions:

- Do we need signed serialized contexts at transport layer for high-sensitivity customers? (security team concern)
- Should SDKs expose a single global adapter instance or allow per-route override for advanced customers? Current plan: global per-process adapter, route override allowed via middleware config.

Related work:

This depends on ENG-41239 (slim-context-bridge-and-loss-tolerant-kv-windowing) for KV cache semantics and is complementary to several instrumentation tickets. We'll also coordinate with the Console team for dashboard placement and with Solutions for SDK docs.
